features.method: Centre fixed by two independent least-squares circle fits to OpenStreetMap geometry that agree to within 0.2 m: (a) OSM way 21825283 'Booster Ring Road' (closed loop, 25 vertices, fit centre 41.836555,-88.263493, fitted radius 58.7 m, rms 0.8 m; path length 367.9 m, consistent with this road being an access loop inside the ring, not the ring itself); (b) OSM ways 272646259 'Booster Tower West' and 272646261 'Booster Tower East' (92 vertices of two arc-shaped RF-gallery building footprints that hug the ring wall, fit centre 41.836557,-88.263493, fitted radius 69.5 m, rms 7.9 m). Both centres coincide to <1 m. The Booster is sourced as a '474-meter-circumference synchrotron' (src:fermilab-miniboone-flux-paper-2009); this is treated as an implicit circularity statement together with the two independent near-circular OSM tracings (ring-road rms 0.8 m over a 59 m radius, i.e. <2% relative deviation). Radius is set from the sourced circumference (474/(2*pi) = 75.44 m) rather than either fitted OSM radius, since both OSM tracings are physically inside/at the wall of the true beam ring, consistently smaller than the accelerator's own radius by 6-17 m. Distances are great-circle on a sphere of radius 6371008.8 m. Check: the first point of the 8 GeV line in the Main Injector TDR survey (the Booster extraction point), converted with the Fermilab Site Coordinate System, lies 76.3 m from this centre against the 75.44 m radius (1.1 %), an independent confirmation from published survey data; accuracy_m lowered from 30 to 10.

features.method: Plan-view SHAPE computed from the Main Injector TDR (src:fermilab-geo-mi-tdr-1994), then PLACED on the ground with the TDR's own published site coordinates (placement revised 2026-10-25); the ring is not traced in OSM. (1) Lattice from the TDR: eight straight sections in the order MI-60, -62, -10, -22, -30, -32, -40, -52 with lengths 138, 52, 69, 52, 138, 52, 69, 52 m (ch. 2 s2.1: 'Straight sections MI-10 and MI-40 are 69 m long (two cells), straight sections MI-22, -32, -52, and -62 are 52 m long (one and one half cells), and straight sections MI-30 and MI-60 are 138 m long (four cells)'), each flanked on both sides by 4 dispersion-suppressor half-cells of 12.9665 m (two 4.1 m dipoles each); the arcs are made of normal half-cells of 17.2886 m (two 6.1 m dipoles each). The number of normal half-cells between successive straights is 2, 12, 38, 2 for each half ring (counted from the dipole positions in the MAD lattice listing in the TDR's appendix; the second half repeats it by the TDR's 'twofold rotational symmetry'). Summed length 3319.414 m against the TDR's 'Circumference 3319.419 m' (Table 1-1). (2) Bending: the dipoles (216 x 6.1 m + 128 x 4.1 m, one 'Dipole Field 17.2 kG') are treated as one field, so each bends by its length / rho with rho = 1842.4 m / 2 pi = 293.2 m; heading was integrated along the sequence (bend spread evenly over each half-cell). The path closes on itself. (3) Self-check against a TDR statement that was NOT used to build the shape: 'The line from MI-52 to MI-62 is offset 28.789277 m from the MI-60 straight section and parallel to it'; the reconstruction gives offsets of 28.74 m and 28.89 m (mean 28.82 m, 0.1% from the TDR) and a direction within 0.02 degrees of MI-60. (4) Placement. The TDR appendix "Main Injector Ring Site Coordinates (MI_19)" is a MAD survey listing of every lattice element in Fermilab site coordinates (X = site north, Z = site east, metres; checked against the NuMI TDR beam sheet, whose first row Q606 is the same point as lattice element M_606, 97163.814 ft north = 29615.590 m). The lattice origin (the middle of the MI-60 straight section) is at X = 29606.625709 m, Z = 30942.395446 m with heading theta = 2.596497 rad. The scanned listing is OCR-damaged; the 89 rows whose digits read cleanly (element, arc length, X, Z) were used. A rotation plus translation (no scaling) of the shape above to those 89 site-coordinate positions leaves an rms residual of 0.34 m (maximum 0.52 m), and puts the lattice origin 0.5 m from the listed one. The site coordinates are converted to WGS 84 with the Fermilab Site Coordinate System of Beams-doc-1148 (origin A0 = 41°50′14.312704″ N, 88°15′41.143123″ W, false x = y = 100000 ft, +y at geodetic azimuth 38°16′48.01429″, scale 1.000029251; a rotated tangent plane on the GRS80 ellipsoid, within 0.2 m of the double stereographic projection near A0). Result: the MI-60 straight of the drawn ring has geodetic azimuth 339.6 deg; Beams-doc-1148 Appendix A gives its FSCS azimuth as 301°13′53.9″, which is 339.51 deg geodetic (0.1 deg, 1.7 m over 1 km, inside the fit residual). Independent confirmations that were not used in the fit: (a) the 8 GeV line survey in the same appendix (P8_GEV) ends at DUSAF x = 99699.211 ft, y = 97317.148 ft, which falls 1.2 m from this ring at path length 588 m, inside the MI-10 straight (570.5 to 639.7 m); the same point is 9.6 m from the earlier placement, at a position in the arc before the straight; (b) the start of that line (the Booster extraction point, x = 99511.383 ft, y = 99309.844 ft) falls 0.9 m from the 75.44 m radius circle of the Booster ring (circumference 474 m) drawn on this map, which validates the conversion to WGS 84; (c) the same conversion places the upstream end of the MINOS enclosure (NuMI TDR beam sheet) 79 m from the OSM MINOS Service Building, and the MINOS paper says the detector cart is pulled about 80 m from the shaft base into the hall. Replaces an earlier placement by a fit to the OSM service road 'Indian Creek Road', which a ring road cannot fix in rotation: it was displaced 38 to 74 m (mean 54 m) from this one and rotated by 5.7 degrees. Sampled every 12 m (278 vertices, chord error 0.06 m); haversine on R = 6371008.8 m measures 3317.4 m, 0.06 % below the TDR circumference (the spherical earth model used for distances here is smaller than the ellipsoid). The tunnel is drawn from the design lattice; as-built deviations of a few metres are possible, so accuracy_m is 8.
features.name: Fermilab Main Injector ring (shape from the TDR lattice, placed with the TDR site coordinates)

provenance.locator: TDR FERMILAB-DESIGN-1994-01 ch. 1 Table 1-1 and ch. 2 s2.1 (straight sections, symmetry), appendix "Main Injector Ring Site Coordinates (MI_19)" (MAD survey table); Beams-doc-1148 section 4.2 (FSCS definition) and Appendix A (MI-60 azimuth)
provenance.note: The shape is the TDR's own geometry and its position is fitted to 89 TDR site-coordinate rows (rms 0.34 m) and converted with the published Fermilab Site Coordinate System; still 'derived' because the shape is computed from the lattice and the survey table was read from a scanned page, and accuracy_m 8 allows for design versus as-built and the NAD83/WGS 84 tie.

features.method: Derived. Radius 1002.68 m = the sourced circumference 6.3 km / 2 pi (Shiltsev: "circumference of 6.3 km"); a circle because the Tevatron shared the Main Ring tunnel and circumference and the MI-60 relation below fits it (no primary source consulted says "circular"). Centre from the Main Injector TDR relation quoted in Beams-doc-1148 Appendix A: the MI-60 straight "is parallel to the Tevatron F0 straight section", its reference point "is 13.222 m downstream from the F0 TeV point, and offset from the TeV straight section by 11.823 m". The MI-60 reference point is the lattice origin of the TDR site-coordinate table (DUSAF x = 101516.842 ft, y = 97134.405 ft, heading 148.76849 deg ccw from site east, i.e. geodetic azimuth 339.5 deg); the F0 point is 13.222 m upstream of it along the heading and 11.823 m to the right (the Main Injector lies south-west of the Tevatron), and the ring centre is a radius further along the right-hand normal. Site coordinates were converted with the FSCS of Beams-doc-1148. Result: centre 41.831643 N, 88.252077 W. Independent test, not used in the placement: the published A0 point (the origin of the site grid, on the Tevatron/Main Ring A0 straight) lies 999.7 m from this centre against the 1002.68 m radius. The earlier placement came from a circle fit to OSM service roads (centre 41.831724 N, 88.251594 W, rms 57 m); it is 41 m from this one. The OSM CDF Hall and D0 Assembly buildings lie 1017.7 m and 1032.1 m from the centre, 15 m and 30 m outside the ring, as surface buildings beside the underground collision halls should; the two distance checks that took them for ring points were removed. Accuracy 10 m: A0 residual 3 m, the 2.7 m between a 1000 m and a 1002.68 m radius, and design versus as-built positions.

provenance.locator: Main Injector TDR FERMILAB-DESIGN-1994-01 (lattice origin, site-coordinate table) and Beams-doc-1148 Appendix A (MI-60 and F0 relation) and section 4.2 (FSCS); circumference per src:fermilab-tevatron-shiltsev-2011, Introduction

summary.plain: Fermilab's main campus near Chicago, where the Booster and (until 2011) the Tevatron ring are drawn to scale from their sourced sizes, along with the Main Injector and Recycler ring, the CDF, D0, MINOS, NOvA, MiniBooNE, MicroBooNE, SBND and ICARUS detector sites and the Muon g-2 MC-1 building. The NuMI beamline and its underground halls are drawn from the NuMI design report's published coordinates; the Booster Neutrino Beam target is a derived point reconstructed from building positions and the sourced MiniBooNE distance. The 3.3 km Main Injector and Recycler ring (one shared tunnel, an oval with eight straight sections, shape from the design handbook) is drawn; PIP-II, Mu2e, the DUNE near detector and a few fixed-target detector halls could not be located precisely and are listed as unlocated. Arrows show the inferred direction of the NuMI and LBNF neutrino beams toward their far detectors in Minnesota and South Dakota, which are shown on separate maps.

unlocated.backlog: Fetch the PIP-II CDR (FERMILAB-DESIGN-2017-01) or TDR civil chapter from a mirror other than lss.fnal.gov; or the IWAA 2024 talk (Bocean) with its site-layout slide read by a person and a published azimuth/coordinate of the linac front end; or re-check OSM once PIP-II civil works are mapped (a landuse=construction polygon near the Booster would anchor the 215 m straight section).
unlocated.reason: PIP-II is under construction 'in a new tunnel with new service buildings and connected to the present Booster through a new transfer line' (src:fermilab-geo-pip-ii-radiation-2018), with a site-plan figure referenced 'with respect to Fermilab Wilson Hall'; the 2024 alignment paper adds that the tunnel 'consists of a straight section and a curved section' with 'a total beam length of approximately 550 meters' (src:fermilab-geo-pip2-iwaa2024-krawczuk) and the 2024 alignment talk gives a 210 m linac tunnel and a 300 m transfer line. No coordinates, azimuth value or dimensioned site plan could be fetched (the official CDR/TDR on lss.fnal.gov returns HTTP 403; the IWAA 2024 slides carry the site layout as an image only; an OSM extract of the campus fetched 2026-10-25 holds no PIP-II way).

unlocated.backlog: The LBNF beamline lattice or site plan in Fermilab site coordinates (FSCS/DUSAF, convertible with Beams-doc-1148 exactly as the NuMI beam sheet was): 'MI-10 Extraction Details' (LBNE-doc-10586) and the Near Site drawings (LBNE-doc-10831) are on the Fermilab DocDB (not public to scripts); an IWAA alignment paper for the LBNF beamline; or OSM mapping of the embankment and the service buildings LBNF-5, -20, -30 and -40 once they are added. The ND hall is 166 ft x 63 ft with its long axis at 90 degrees to the beam (ND CDR Table 8.1, DUNE TDR Vol. II).
unlocated.reason: No published coordinate for the LBNF target, target hall or near-detector hall was found. Published at design stage: the beam is extracted at MI-10 (LBNF CDR Vol. 3, arXiv:1601.05823); "transported 328 m (1078 ft) to the LBNF Target Complex (to the target)" (section 5.3.2) against "approximately 1,200 feet from the extraction at MI-10 to the Target Hall" (section 6.2.7) and about 1,000 ft in DOE/EA-1943; "The overall bend of the proton beam is 7.2o westward and 5.8o downward" (arXiv:1704.04471). With the Main Injector now placed from the TDR site coordinates, the MI-10 straight has heading 280.5 deg and 280.5 + 7.2 = 287.7 deg equals the great-circle bearing from MI-10 to the SURF caverns (287.76 deg), which supports the layout geometry but fixes no position: where the beam leaves the 69 m straight, which of the path lengths (305, 328 or 366 m) is as built and where the bend occurs leave the target about 50 m uncertain (chains of these figures put it at lon -88.2720 to -88.2734, lat 41.8326 to 41.8331, and the ND hall at lon -88.2786 to -88.2800, lat 41.8341 to 41.8347, from 37 m west to 78 m east of Kirk Road across the combinations, against the EA's 38-46 m from the hall's closest point). Not drawn: that is a design-stage estimate, not a position.

unlocated.reason: The original DAMIC prototype's Fermilab placement (2008-2012) has no dedicated hall coordinate in the sources consulted (checked 2026-09-18); the existing placement record notes only that a precise coordinate was not found.

unlocated.reason: No dedicated OpenStreetMap footprint or other sourced coordinate for the DONUT hall was found (checked 2026-09-18); the existing placement record for this 1997 fixed-target experiment cites only a Wikipedia pointer.

unlocated.backlog: Same backlog as beamline:lbnf: once the target (or the hall) has a published site coordinate, the hall follows from 574 m along the bearing to SURF (287.7 deg) and its 166 ft x 63 ft size.
unlocated.reason: The DUNE near detector hall is sourced at 574 m ("about 570 m") from the LBNF target, 60 m deep, "on the western-most boundary of Fermi National Laboratory" and "125-150 feet east of Kirk Road at its closest point" (DOE/EA-1943), 166 ft x 63 ft with its long axis at 90 degrees to the beam (ND CDR Table 8.1; DUNE TDR Vol. II); but the LBNF target it is measured from has no published coordinate (see beamline:lbnf), and chaining the figures leaves the hall about 50 m uncertain, too coarse for a 50 m hall.

unlocated.backlog: Search the KTeV design report (INSPIRE literature 345348) for a hall/beamline number that could be matched to a Fermilab fixed-target-area site plan.
unlocated.reason: No OpenStreetMap footprint or other sourced coordinate for the KTeV hall was found (checked 2026-09-18; a targeted OSM name search for 'KTeV' returned no results).

unlocated.backlog: The MINERvA detector paper (NIM A743, arXiv:1305.5199) section on the detector location for the offset of its upstream face from the hall's upstream end; the hall is 150 ft long and the TDR puts the MINOS detector face 85.5 ft inside it, so MINERvA sits in the first ~85 ft.
unlocated.reason: MINERvA stood in the MINOS near-detector hall, which is now drawn (geometry:fermilab-minos-near-hall, from the NuMI TDR beam sheet); the NuMI paper confirms the cavern "subsequently housed additional experiments such as MINERvA or ArgoNeuT". The position of the MINERvA detector inside the hall is not published in a source fetched.

unlocated.backlog: A candidate building, OSM way 720556732 'MC-2' (drawn as context only, geometry:fermilab-mc2-building), stands 84 m from the confirmed MC-1/g-2 building and is plausible given the MC-1/MC-2 naming pattern, but no fetchable text confirms MC-2 is specifically the Mu2e hall (checked 2026-09-18: a web search and two attempts to read arXiv:2208.02889 'Muon Campus at Fermilab', HTML and PDF). Re-checked 2026-10-25: the Mu2e TDR (arXiv:1501.05241, Fig. 6.120 and sections 1-2) and the Muon Campus overview (arXiv:2208.02889) contain no site coordinate and do not name the Mu2e building MC-2; further web searches for 'MC-2' with Mu2e found no source. The former Antiproton Source buildings AP-0/AP-10/AP-30/AP-50 (OSM, src:fermilab-geo-osm-muon-campus) cluster near 41.8346,-88.2656 and are candidate anchors for the adjacent Delivery Ring (ex-Debuncher), but no source consulted (checked 2026-09-18) states the ring's shape or circumference, and three building centroids are not enough to justify drawing a ring without a sourced vertex/side correspondence, so it is not drawn. Confirming either would let Mu2e become a drawn `hall`. Next: Fermilab's facilities directory or a Muon Campus site plan that names the Mu2e building, or the Mu2e Offline geometry text files (world coordinates of the hall).
unlocated.reason: No OpenStreetMap footprint is confirmed for the Mu2e building specifically (a targeted OSM name search for 'Mu2e' found none); the Mu2e TDR (src:muons-arxiv-1501-05241) describes the production/transport/detector solenoid dimensions and states the Mu2e building shares a berm/enclosure with the Delivery Ring extraction beamline (the M4 beamline), but gives no single coordinate or scalar distance from a fixed point.
